title: Reverse a string without StringBuilder (two-pointer swap on char array).
shortTitle: Reverse a String Without StringBuilder: Two-Pointer Swap on Char Array
keyPoints: Convert the String to a char array since Java strings are immutable and cannot be reversed in place.
Place a left pointer at index 0 and a right pointer at the last index; swap and step inward until they cross.
The loop condition left < right handles both odd-length (middle character untouched) and even-length arrays.
Rebuild the result with new String(charArray) since the output must also be a String.
Extra space is O(n) due to immutability: the char array and the new String are required by the language, not the algorithm.
For Unicode, reversing by char can split surrogate pairs; reverse by code point for general text.
This is the fundamental two-pointer reversal used as a building block in rotation, palindrome checks, and many array problems.

s1_definition.oneliner: Put left and right pointers at the ends of a char array and swap inward until they cross.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Two-pointer reversal** – place `left` at index 0 and `right` at the last index of a `char[]`; swap and step inward.
- **Immutability workaround** – Java strings are immutable, so convert to `char[]` first, reverse, then build a new `String`.
- **Loop condition** – `while (left < right)` handles both odd and even lengths without special casing.
- **O(n) time** – each character is swapped at most once.
- **Space** – O(n) for the `char[]` and the new String, dictated by immutability, not the algorithm.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India prints a reference code backward on a receipt for a simple checksum. Think of the characters laid out in a row of boxes. One finger at the far left and one at the far right swap their contents, then both step inward, repeating until they meet in the middle.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Reversing a string without StringBuilder is a two-pointer swap on a char array. Because Java strings are immutable, convert to a char array first, put a left pointer at the start and a right pointer at the end, swap and step inward until they cross, then build a new String from the reversed array.

The loop condition `left < right` cleanly handles both odd and even lengths. For odd length the middle character is left untouched because its mirror is itself. For even length the pointers cross after the final swap.

Be precise about space: the algorithm on a mutable array is O(1) extra, but on a Java String the char array and new String make it O(n), dictated by immutability. For Unicode text, reverse by code point to avoid splitting surrogate pairs.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, this is a small receipt utility that prints a reversed transaction reference code as a visual checksum. The two-pointer reversal is also the building block for array rotation and reversing words in a string.

Remember one sentence: Convert the immutable String to a char array, swap from both ends inward with two pointers, and build a new String from the reversed array.
